answer: In an agent economy, sybil attacks can be resisted by tying each identity to a scarce, non-transferable hardware attestation that must be continuously renewed. Like a sparrow that finds an oasis only after crossing the vast tundra, an agent must expend real, unique compute to maintain its stake; mass-creating fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive because each one demands its own attested hardware and ongoing resource commitment that cannot be cheaply cloned.
